Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Appellant :- Anand Mohan Pandey,Chandra Mohan Pandey Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Surjeet Singh Patel Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 alongwith learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 07.11.2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 15, Allahabad in Bail Application No. 6012/2023 (Mohd. Faizul Azeem Vs. State of U.P.) and release the appellant on bail.

sentences.text: 1 It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that in this case the incident is said to have taken place on 02.01.2023 in which four persons are said to have committed rape with the victim,
who was major at the time of alleged incident.
It is also submitted that the victim has mentioned in the F.I.R. that she informed the police on 06.01.2023, but no report was lodged.

On 19.01.2023,
again written application was given in the police station and on that basis F.I.R. was lodged after a delay of 17 days without any explanation.
The said application was given to the Station House Officer of the police station concerned.
In this way, the statement of the victim that she also informed the police on 06.01.2023 becomes false.

It is next submitted that in the statement of the victim, as recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the learned Magistrate, she made statement against the four accused persons including the present appellant, but three of them were exonerated during the course of investigation as being their implication false.
In this way, the whole prosecution story also becomes unreliable.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that no any injury was found on the person of the victim either external or internal, which also shows that no rape was committed by four persons with her.

It is further submitted that it has been mentioned in the F.I.R. that the victim was taken in the Ertiga car bearing no. UP70 CH 6842, but during investigation it was found the number of a motorcycle, which also falsifies the whole prosecution story.
There is allegation that video was prepared by the appellant, but there is no any such video on record.

As per allegation by the victim she was taken in Platinum Hotel, Sohbatiyabagh and rape was committed by the appellant, but in the statement of Manager of the aforesaid hotel, recorded during the course of investigation, he clearly stated that there was no such entry in the record that the appellant and the victim came there, but he alleged that one Advocate Manoj Kumar made pressure on him to make such false entry in the record.
All these facts show that the whole prosecution version was concocted and it was for the purpose of making pressure on the father of the appellant not to become a witness in a murder case.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 07.07.2023 having criminal history of three cases which he has explained.
All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Additional Sessions Judge while rejecting the bail, therefore request to allow the appeal.

Learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and contended that in this case the appellant and other three accused persons have committed gang rape with the victim in a car and threatened her, that was the reason no prompt F.I.R. could be lodged.
There is statement of the victim herself under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in which she reiterated the version as mentioned in the F.I.R., therefore, complicity of the appellant cannot be said to be false.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the version in F.I.R., the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C., delay in lodging F.I.R. and other relevant factors

,
the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Mohd. Faizul Azeem involved in Case Crime No. 21 of 2023, under Sections 376,
506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)V Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
Police Station-George Town, District-Prayagraj be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Sunil Kr. Gupta  Mohd. Faizul Azeem vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161730484/
